Having pronounced this curse on Rambha, the rishi became

Ramhha having been instantly turned to stone, Indra and

Shti Vishwamitra having lost the merit of his penances could 
obtain no peace ; his passions remaining unsubdued, he resolved 
to speak no word to any and never give way to anger ; he said : 
" For a thousand years, I will not breathe. Reducing my body 
to the last extremity, mastering my senses, I will obtain 
brahmanhood by the power of my penance. Measurdess years, 
shall I remain standing, neither breathing nor eating, even should 
my limbs become atrophied." 
0 Rama, Vishwamitra resolved to perform this mortification

In distress, they addressed Shri Brahma saying : " 0 Lord,

has persisted in his practices aud is free from desire and aversion. 
If thou dost not grant him brahmanhood, verily the three worlds 
will be destroyed. None can find rest anywhere, the seas are

austerities; the sun is deprived of its splendour, the earth is 
agitated and the wind stirs not. 0 Lord, we cannot move him 
from his resolve. On account of this peril, men like atheists

Tbe divine sage then psid homage to the great Vasishtba and,

0 Raghava, verily he is the chief of sages and the personification 
of Yoga. Constantly engaged in acts of virtue, he still performs 
rigorous penances." 
Having uttered these words, Shri Shatanands becsme silent. 
When this excellent sage had ended his narrative, King Janaka

0 Muni, thou hast, by thy presence, done us great honour.

brief.summary_1line: After a thousand years of extreme austerities and restraint, Vishwamitra is finally recognized by Brahma and Vasistha as a Brahmarishi.

image_candidates.scene_text: Emaciated Vishwamitra stands motionless in austerity as smoke rises from his head, shaking the three worlds.
Indra disguised as a humble brahmin receives the only meal prepared by the silent sage Vishwamitra.
Brahma and the assembled gods appear before the ascetic and proclaim him a Brahmarishi while he bows in reverence.

deep.rich_summary: After cursing the celestial nymph Rambha in anger, Vishwamitra regrets that wrath has ruined the fruit of his austerities. Determined to conquer anger and desire completely, he undertakes an even harsher vow: a thousand years of silence, breath control, and extreme asceticism. When that period ends and he finally prepares to eat, Indra—disguised as a brahmin—begs for the food, and Vishwamitra gives it away without speaking. He resumes his penance for another thousand years, generating such intense spiritual power that smoke rises from his head and the cosmos begins to tremble. Alarmed, the gods beg Brahma to grant him brahmanhood. Brahma appears and proclaims Vishwamitra a Brahmarishi. At Vishwamitra’s request, the sage Vasishta acknowledges him as such, resolving their long rivalry and completing Vishwamitra’s transformation from king to supreme sage.

highlight_spans.why: Vishwamitra’s curse on Rambha shows how even great ascetics can lose spiritual merit through anger.
His vow to remain silent and master breath for a thousand years marks the turning point in his quest for absolute self‑control.
The terrifying smoke rising from his head symbolizes the cosmic power generated by his austerities.
Brahma’s proclamation recognizing Vishwamitra as a Brahmarishi fulfills his long struggle for spiritual supremacy.
Vasishta’s acceptance of Vishwamitra as a Brahmarishi resolves their historic rivalry and confirms his transformation.

top_scenes.scene_text: The ascetic Vishwamitra stands unmoving in extreme penance as smoke rises from his head, shaking the heavens while gods watch in fear.
Brahma descends with the assembled gods before the emaciated sage and proclaims Vishwamitra a Brahmarishi.
Indra disguised as a humble brahmin receives the only meal of the silent Vishwamitra after a thousand years of austerity.
